steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Meine Dame, you should rest.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Just how many times have you repainted this already? If you're reworking the piece, then why not...

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Why not have me contact the art gallery and ask them to delay the exhibition?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: You've been so much more spirited since that musician arrived. But to jump straight back into painting when you've yet to fully recover from your illness, only to work on... this piece...

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Is this a... night sky? The blacks are so intense I can't make anything out.
What a truly unforgettable shade of night. I see your painting will soon be complete.
However, the intense emotions fueling your tireless endeavors are also wearing down your body, and you're in no shape to go on.
So... would you like me to continue my performance?
Alright, I've heard your answer.
As well as your pain, regret, remorse, obsession... In your heart, Leithanien died alongside you that night. The very same night reflected in your painting.
Then allow me to play you a dirge, albeit more than twenty years late.
Leithanien's capital, Zwillingstürme, city center

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: Listen.

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: Every day at this hour, this city is filled with all kinds of music.

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: Students stopping by the instrument shops on the way home from school, discussing which of the new instruments has a more stable circuit.

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: Pedestrians getting off work, slowing their pace as their coins jingle into a instrument case in front of a street artist.

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: Young lovers clinking together glasses of wine in restaurants, and stoves steaming in warm homes.

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: Every scene as touching as the last.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Evenings in Zwillingstürme have always been a source of inspiration for many great musicians.

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: Hmm... Then shall we add a few more pieces to the program for the celebration?

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: Every year we begin with the Güldenesgesatz, and then perform the same routine classical pieces after. Surely the people are becoming less and less interested by the year?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: As ever, the program is up to Your Majesties to decide.

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: Then let's have a chat with the conductor and the principals after this.

steps.name: Golden-haired Woman
steps.text: By the way, I recall you mentioning that you brought a young lady to see me.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Ja, Your Majesty.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: This is Viviana, Werner's daughter.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Pleased to make your acquaintance, Ewigegnade—Your Majesty.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Ah, even better than expected. Are you still getting used to Leithanien after your return from Kazimierz?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I am grateful for your concern. Leithanien is... far more elegant and beautiful than I remember.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: No need to be so formal. Cora and I often meet outside the Spires for a chat, like the one we're having now.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You must still be in mourning over Werner's recent passing. If we had the luxury of time, I'd much rather you have a chance to relax in the city first.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You mean, before you appoint me as—

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: An Empresses' Voice.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: As you've heard from Cora, this was Werner's request.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I am... truly honored by the opportunity.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: The nobles prefer to send me their youngest sons when they're about ten years of age, but I believe you're fully qualified for the position.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: And after meeting you in person, I'm even more sure of it.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You praise me too highly.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Modesty is a virtue, but so is the courage to speak your mind.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: While I'd be more than glad to fulfill your father's request, I'd also like to hear your own thoughts on this.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: How do you truly feel about yourself, about Leithanien, and about the future before us?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Your Majesty, I was not aware that you would be entertaining a guest.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: It's fine, Brandt. This is the time I told you to come over, after all. Tell me about your findings in Sturmland.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Their copy of the Güldenesgesatz was stolen from the Kurfürst's spire.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The thieves are most likely part of the same group behind the Kurfürst's assassination, who call themselves the 'Echoes of Herkunftshorn.'

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Herkunftshorn... The Genesis Horn. Now that's a name I haven't heard in a long time.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...The Witch King's remains.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: I interrogated one of their men. They have sent the copy to Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: To this very city...

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Cora, how many years have we done Das Kaiserinnensfest?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: This year will be the twenty-third, Your Majesty.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: So he's been dead for twenty-three years now.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: How many of these people working tirelessly in his name have even seen him with their own eyes?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: It's something I've always found saddening. Just what is it about the Leithanien of today that fills them with so much resentment?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Resentment has never been rational, Your Majesty.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Perhaps I should call off this year's event.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: If they really intend on using the Movement to cause chaos in the capital... I don't want anyone who came for the celebration to come to any harm.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: We still have three days to go.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: I will find them and retrieve it.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: I should have dispatched several Voices to work on this together.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Allow me, Your Majesty.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The Empresses' Voice represents the glory and majesty of the Kaiserinnen, so if they were to suddenly show up across the city, they will naturally attract the attention of both civilians and the enemy.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But I... Or rather, what the people know me for has nothing whatsoever to do with this matter.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: An interesting proposal.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Your Majesty, I believe we shouldn't let an untrained—

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Brandt Reiner. I'm sure you and Viviana will be enough to solve this problem for me.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Also... Another Voice has just brought back a couple of interesting pieces from Kreis Wasserland. Ask Hildegard if she would like to come by my tower for a listening session.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: After all, you're going to go see her after this, yes?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...Ja, Your Majesty.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Grandmaster Ioleta has taught you well. I have a feeling you'll be my favorite Voice.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Danke schön.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Anyway, I don't need an answer today, but I'll allow you to act as an Empresses' Voice in the meantime. Of course, any new Voices will only officially enter the Spires after the celebrations are over, as per usual.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Until then, I'll be anticipating your answer.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: My true feelings...

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Sadly, our meeting has been as brief as a sunset.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Ah, hold on.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: It's time. Do you see it?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The... fountain in the plaza?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Beautiful, no?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: It is not simply water splashing along to a melody. The flowing water is itself the medium playing it.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I've heard that many of the buildings and streets in Zwillingstürme are themselves instruments.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Back in the day, I took a bit of time to figure out a way to keep them stable for decades. It seems that was time well spent.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So you designed them personally?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Viviana, no matter what choice you make in the end...

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: I do hope you'll fall in love with this place, as I have.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Until then, let Zwillingstürme's afterglow bring you some solace.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...The afterglow.
She had often imagined what kind of city Zwillingstürme would be like.
She had a good guess from the novels and poems she read as a child.
She understood what it really looked like from the news and foreign television programs.
But only now does she stand in the center of the capital for the first time, experiencing the city's lights and shadows, its sounds and scents.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Colors out of a classical painting.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The timbre of accordions playing.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And the fragrance of marigolds.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's just like a living poem... Surprisingly, the evening in Zwillingstürme is exactly how I imagined it.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You didn't need to involve yourself in this.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Her Majesty never gave me a chance to excuse myself before they spoke about it. Which means I was already involved.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Besides, there are things I'm curious about too.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You want to uncover the truth behind your father's death.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Not just that.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I also wish to... find myself, within the darkness about to descend upon us.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Then, are you already prepared to step into the night?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Before I returned, I gave away my entire book collection to a friend of mine.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: She, too, had just returned to the homeland that once expelled her, and carried with her a certain conviction.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I'm sure you'll laugh at me for saying this, but back then, I imagined countless times how she must have felt at that moment.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And now, I think I have the slightest inkling of that feeling.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: You have concerns about Lieselotte's decision.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The Empresses' Voices chosen by Ewigegnade have always been qualified, and I will not question her judgement in that regard.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Frau Viviana Droste is an excellent caster. I've seen recordings of her skilled manipulations of candleflames and shadows.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: But... her experience in handling actual crises may be lacking. After all, all of her experience in battle has occurred on artificial stages.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Brandt Reiner.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Your allegiance no longer lies with the Hochberg family.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...No one is more aware of that than I, Your Majesty.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Otherwise, I wouldn't have simply stood there with a blank stare that night, twenty-three years ago.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: I lost the right to choose long ago. The blade and Arts of a Gesatzswächter belong only to the Güldenesgesatz and to Leithanien.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: The Güldenesgesatz, and Leithanien.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: What if you could only choose one?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The Güldenesgesatz defines Leithanien. In over a thousand years, the two have never diverged.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: The Movement's melody was created by Leithanians, and it's hardly impossible to alter it.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Herkunftshorn certainly did.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Bearing but one part of the responsibility necessarily means abandoning the others.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Think it through, Brandt. No one in this land can refuse to make a choice forever.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: I will... carefully consider your words.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: There is one more thing. Ewigegnade wanted me to ask if you were free to listen to a performance by the Empresses' Voices.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: I will be.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Lieselotte will probably have fallen asleep by the time I head over, though.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Michael.
Your Majesty. First things first, I don't want to go to the spire next door for dinner on your behalf anymore. I'm sure you know she doesn't like me at all.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Enough of your jests.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Continue keeping an eye on the happenings in the city.
Do you need me to 'cooperate' with the Gesatzswächter and the... unofficial Empresses' Voice? Or the opposite?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: I already told you.
'Continue,' right? Got it.

steps.name: Art Gallery Spectator
steps.text: Did you see that just now?

steps.name: Art Gallery Spectator
steps.text: Frau Seemann, she... and those black paintings too.

steps.name: Art Gallery Spectator
steps.text: How horrid!

steps.name: Art Gallery Spectator
steps.text: Everyone's saying that it's a curse from His Majesty...

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Move, all of you. Don't crowd in here.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: The road ahead is closed, and the gallery will not be opened to the public today.
Send a reply to Graf Josef. The Gendarmerie will bear the costs of the gallery's damages.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Ja, Captain Loris.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Right, did you save the contact details of the fräulein who lost her necklace the other day? That girl's the editor-in-chief for the Kunst der Zwillingstürme.

spans.text: Right, did you save the contact details of the fräulein who lost her necklace the other day? That girl's the editor-in-chief for the

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Please ask her to leave some space in their next issue for a presentation on, well, Frau Seemann's 'posthumous work.'

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: A... presentation?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Invite the critics to use their imaginations.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Frau Seemann was creating a new work with her blood, sweat and tears, and unfortunately ended up also giving her life to the canvas and succumbing to exhaustion—Her final piece is certainly deserving of some sort of praise.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: 'Unfortunately, this incomplete masterpiece will not be exhibited to the public, as per her final wishes.'

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I can only hope for the article to have no mention of His Majesty's name.
So... what do you think is the actual reason for Frau Seemann's demise?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Who let you in...?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Wait, the C-Candle..!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Technically, the title issued by the Kazimierz Knights Association no longer belongs to me after retirement.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: I don't care what the Kazimierzians think!

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: A few years back, when they were hiding you in the snow, I wrote a few letters of protest to the Nova Knightclub! And when I later found out about your retirement, I drowned myself in drink for a few days, behind the Captain's back.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: So that's why you were slacking off back then?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: But I'll overlook it, for the sake of our distinguished guest.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Guten Tag, Vizegraf Loris Bordin.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: A pleasure to meet you.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Pym, pass the order: this lovely lady is the gallery's sole visitor of the day. Tell the men to keep watch outside, and not to interfere with her movements.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: R-Right away, sir!

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: When Frau Löwenstein greeted me earlier, I had no idea Their Majesties had actually appointed another special envoy.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I hope you can keep this a secret.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Please rest assured.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Although... this is such a small accident, so why did it spring the Kaiserin's secret envoy into action?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: An accident? Is that the conclusion of the Gendarmerie's investigation?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: We did the forensics, and Frau Seemann did indeed die from exhaustion.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: According to her attendant, she went without food or rest for multiple days on end.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I can't help but admire her spirit. Such a dedicated artist is hard to come by, even in Leithanien.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: This work must have been extremely important to her then.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Frau Seeman has not presented a new work for more than two decades.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: She then suddenly decided to work on this painting, even notifying the gallery in advance that would personally unveil it today, on the first day of the exhibition.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I'm sure you know what happened next. When the audience arrived, they were greeted only by the artist collapsing in front of her painting.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: What about the painting itself?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Was it... completed?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: A difficult question to answer.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You'd better see it with your own eyes. I can only say that its subject was... an unexpected surprise.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Is this a brochure for the exhibition?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Der Tod des Hexenkönigs—Did the artist title her work before completing it?

spans.text: —Did the artist title her work before completing it?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: To be honest, many of the visitors came rushing here just because of the name.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I'd have thought Leithanien would find it quite unwelcome.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I'm guessing you haven't been here for long?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Mhm. I only just returned a little while ago.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: No wonder. You may not be aware, but the fall of His Majesty is an enormously popular subject these days. Even counting operas alone, there are over a hundred depicting how the Kaiserinnen miraculously triumphed over their enemy.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: How careless of me. So the actual protagonists of these stories are Their Majesties.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Haha. In Leithanien, you're free to create anything, so... this is probably the result of the people revealing their true feelings.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Frau Seemann may have also wanted to take the celebration as a chance to add a bit of luster to this national holiday, by working with such a classic theme.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But even so, you said her painting was an 'unexpected surprise'?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: It's up ahead, just around the corner.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Once you've had a look, I think you'll share my hope that this was just an accident.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: An attack?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Please wait here while I check the situation.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I could help you out.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: It might turn out to be just a couple of drunkards on the streets breaking in their new wands, and I'd rather not bother you with something so trifling.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Captain! We triangulated the source of the noise, and it's coming from the alley over there—

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Have you sent anyone over?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: The 2nd squad went in, but no one's come out yet.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...Are they still in there?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: It was the strangest fellow we've ever seen. He definitely heard us rushing over, but it seemed like he was still trying to break into the gallery instead of fleeing.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Could this be something big? Do you want to bring a few more men along, Captain?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: No need for that.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Like I said, it's nothing major. Just some crazy punks stirring up trouble for us to vent their frustrations.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Right, that lady you fancy... the competition knight, what was her surname?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Can...Candle... Droste!

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...A name I've never heard of.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Tell the others to keep the chase while we return to the gallery to make sure Frau Droste hasn't come to any harm.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: A noblewoman with the Kaiserin's trust is far more valuable than all the works and secrets in that gallery combined.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Footsteps?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Is there someone up ahead? Isn't the gallery closed off to the public?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So this is the painting.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And the subject is... the Death of the Witch King?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: No, this isn't Der Tod des Hexenkönigs at all...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: This is... ugh...
Black and disorderly, the lines twist into infinity.
Der Tod des Hexenkönigs sitting at the center isn't the only thing to have those twisted lines painted over it—every other painting on the wall sports the same look.

spans.text: sitting at the center isn't the only thing to have those twisted lines painted over it—every other painting on the wall sports the same look.

steps.text: The black spirals resemble vortices, breaking out of the frames one after another and filling the entire space.
The lines seem to twist and burrow into her eyes, erupting into a series of mournful sobs in the depths of her mind.
Her consciousness is pulled, deformed, fractured, and plunged into chaos.
Shadows sway behind Viviana. She can hardly control her Arts. She wants to preserve herself, to escape.
This terrifying power needs no concrete descriptor, image, or sound to remind anyone of what it is.
Much like its title, it forcefully crams itself directly into its audience's cognition, reflecting its very meaning into their minds—
'The Witch King.'

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What a beautiful piece of art.
A calm voice can suddenly be heard in the center of the exhibition hall.
The noise comes to a halt, and the black spirals retreat into the paintings.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: This painting...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: There's no obvious trace of Originium Arts... so why?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Arts aren't the only thing that can affect the mind.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Something need only be true enough to tug at one's heartstrings, be it a picture or a melody.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But please, don't fear it... feel it.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...It's very intense.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: A rich and deep emotion flows in these seemingly messy brushstrokes.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's... hard to keep looking.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That's because you're looking at a person's soul.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: She put both the Witch King in her heart and her very life onto the canvas.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Frau Seemann... What connection did she have with His Majesty?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: His death changed her entire life.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: As a young woman, she revered the man on the throne. She was in love with a symbol, a god.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And then that god fell right before her eyes.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: She was confused, bewildered by his mortality. She lost her love, her purest emotions, and very nearly her ability to create as well.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: She was... trapped.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And only when her life was nearing its end did she realize this.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You speak as if you were her.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Her innermost emotions resonated with my melody. I went into the depths of her soul and heard her cry for help.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Cry for help?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It's the same everywhere you go.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Many people are trapped in whatever fateful moment changed the course of their lives, walking along an endless spiral staircase.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Just like...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: ...Your father. And you as well.
